title: How do we write huge populations using powers of ten?
description: The starlings and mosquitoes of the world are written with one digit before the point, times a power of ten. Then dividing the number of people by the number of African elephants is checked against twenty thousand. Keeko doubts the count of places for the mosquitoes.
teaching_notes: One idea: the hops of the point give the power of ten, and dividing powers of ten subtracts the powers. Watch for students who count the zeroes of the name and forget the digits in front of them.

source: Write the starling and mosquito populations in scientific notation, and check the people for every African elephant
video_script.why: A huge count is clearer as one digit before the point times a power of ten, and the power comes from counting the hops of the point.
video_script.substitution: Write the number in full, count the hops of the point to sit after the first digit, and use the count as the power of ten.
video_script.anchor: starlings, mosquitoes, people and African elephants of the world
video_script.wrong_answer: one point one times ten to the power thirteen
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko counts the 12 zeroes of a trillion and adds 1, giving 10 to the power 13. But 110 trillion has 15 digits, so the point hops 14 places and the power is 14; using 13 makes the number ten times too small.
video_script.payoff_line: The hops of the point give the power of ten, and dividing subtracts the powers

final_answer.value: 1.3 × 10 to the power 9 starlings, 1.1 × 10 to the power 14 mosquitoes, and yes, about 20000 people per elephant
final_answer.spoken: The starlings number one point three times ten to the power nine. The mosquitoes number one point one times ten to the power fourteen. Yes, there are about twenty thousand people for every African elephant.

maths_rules: the slip: 1.1 × 10¹³ is 11 trillion, ten times too small
video_script.design: The two numbers are written in full, one after the other, with the point hopping left and a counter. The division of the two populations is built with the numbers in front first, then the powers of ten.

narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>The hops of the point give the power of ten, and dividing subtracts the powers.
<bookmark mark='ans1'/>One point three billion starlings is one point three times ten to the power nine.
<bookmark mark='mos'/>One hundred ten trillion mosquitoes is one point one times ten to the power fourteen.
<bookmark mark='ans2'/>Nine minus five is four, so the result is two times ten to the power four.
<bookmark mark='twenty'/>That is twenty thousand people for every elephant, so the claim is right.
